summary: A mailing list of the ARPANET liaisons and others who should receive formal documents like RFCs by post in 1971. It names contact people at each site and replaces RFC 95. It was replaced by RFC 168.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 155 is a directory of people and postal addresses for sending RFCs and other formal network documents. It replaced RFC 95 and was later replaced by RFC 168.

subtitle: The people and addresses for distributing early network documents

tldr.problem: People responsible for network sites and other recipients needed to receive the initial distribution of formal documents.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC lists the liaisons and other recipients, with postal addresses, for sending RFCs and related documents.
tldr.outcome: The list superseded RFC 95 and was later replaced by RFC 168.

sections.title: Who Should Receive the Documents
sections.content:
RFC 155 identifies network liaisons and others who should receive the initial distribution of formal documents. The note at the start says the list supersedes RFC 95 and corresponds to the Current Directory of Network Participants.

Most entries give a network site, a named contact and a postal address. The document is a distribution list, not a protocol for transferring documents.
sections.plainLanguage: This document tells senders where to mail formal network papers and who should receive them. It is an address list, not a set of network instructions.

sections.title: Site Contacts and Other Addressees
sections.content:
The main list pairs site names with contacts and their mailing addresses. The RFC also has a separate group of current RFC addressees that are not sites, including organizations and individuals.

A further section lists NIC Station Agents by site. These contacts are distinct from the primary RFC addressees and are identified to support local distribution.
sections.plainLanguage: The list has contacts for network sites, additional recipients who are not sites, and NIC Station Agents. Each entry helps identify a person or organization that should receive documents.

sections.title: Scope and Replacement
sections.content:
The document covers the people who should receive the initial distribution of formal documents. It contains names, organizations and postal addresses; it does not specify how a site must handle or circulate a document after receiving it.

RFC 155 supersedes RFC 95. The unit metadata records RFC 168 as its successor.
sections.plainLanguage: The list covers initial recipients only. RFC 155 replaced an earlier list and was later replaced by RFC 168.
